2	title: "What the Assistant can do"
3	description: "What you can ask the Assistant for, job by job, how it checks its work, and where its limits are."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	The Assistant edits the project in its own window. You ask in plain words, it makes the edits one at a time, and each one lands where you can see it. Almost all of them [can be undone](#each-edit-is-an-undo-step). This page goes through what you can ask for, job by job, and where the limits are.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
12	  keys="⌃⌘A"
13	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
14	  tools={['get_project', 'render_frame', 'undo', 'redo']}
15	  needs="Your own Anthropic API key"
16	/>
17	
18	## The same tools as MCP
19	
20	The Assistant works by calling tools, one for each job. They're the same tools an outside AI agent uses when it connects to Frame Job [over MCP](/mcp/overview/), so anything here is something an agent can do too. There are a few exceptions, listed in [What it won't do](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/), and some tools that write files [ask you first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-asks-about-first).
21	
22	Four tools are always at hand: reading the project, rendering a frame, undo and redo. It finds every other tool by searching for what it wants to do, so you never need to name one. A tool kept from it outright doesn't turn up in that search at all.
23	
24	Each job below lists its tools, because those are the names you'll see in the [tool call lines](/assistant/conversation/#tool-call-lines). [All tools](/mcp/tools/) describes each one.
25	
26	## What you can ask for
27	
28	Ask in your own words, for example "put a title over the first five seconds". You don't need to know which job a request falls under. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/) for how to send one.
29	
30	### Projects and navigation
31	
32	It can open, create and save projects, move the playhead, set the in and out range, change the selection, and enter or leave a nest. It can also make a [new project from a range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) or a [vertical version](/framing/make-vertical-version/).
33	
34	Saving asks first. Making a new project from a range or a vertical version asks first when it names where to save. Moving the playhead, setting the range and changing the selection aren't edits, so they make no undo step.
35	
36	A project it opens or creates gets a window of its own, and the Assistant stays with the project it started in.
37	
38	<AtAGlance tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version', 'save_project', 'set_playhead', 'set_range', 'set_selection', 'set_scope']} />
39	
40	### Tracks, markers and the canvas
41	
42	It can add, remove and reorder tracks, remove the empty ones, rename a track, hide, mute, solo or lock one, and set its [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) and [mix](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). It can add, move, rename and remove [markers](/timeline/markers/), make one a chapter, and set its colour, which you can't do yourself. It can change the canvas's [size](/projects/canvas-size/), [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) and [background](/projects/background-and-timecode/).
43	
44	<AtAGlance tools={['add_track', 'remove_track', 'move_track', 'set_track', 'remove_empty_tracks', 'add_marker', 'set_marker', 'remove_marker', 'set_canvas']} />
45	
46	### Media
47	
48	It can [import](/projects/import-media/), [relink](/projects/relink-media/) and [remove](/projects/remove-media/) media, [copy it into the project](/projects/consolidate-media/) and set a file's [camera log](/hdr/camera-log/). Copying into the project asks first.
49	
50	It can also save where a file's speech is, read the [on-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) of a file, and attach or read a recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/).
51	
52	<AtAGlance tools={['import_media', 'add_media', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'set_media_color', 'set_media_speech', 'consolidate_media', 'get_media_analysis', 'set_media_cursor', 'get_cursor_events']} />
53	
54	### Placing clips
55	
56	It can place media, [text](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/), [shapes](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/), [backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/), [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) and [graphics](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/). It can [insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/), paste and duplicate, and put [text behind a subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).
57	
58	<AtAGlance tools={['add_clip', 'add_text_clip', 'add_shape_clip', 'add_adjustment_clip', 'add_background', 'add_blurred_background', 'text_behind_subject', 'insert_clip', 'overwrite_clip', 'paste', 'duplicate', 'insert_graphic']} />
59	
60	### Editing clips
61	
62	It can [move](/editing/move-clips/), [trim](/editing/trimming/), [split](/editing/splitting/), [slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/), [rate-stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/), [ripple-delete and lift](/editing/delete-clips/), [insert time and close gaps](/editing/close-gaps/). It can [detach audio and attach it again](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and make [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
63	
64	For several cameras or long recordings it can [split at shot changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/), [copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/), [switch a shot's angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [switch by speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/).
65	
66	<AtAGlance tools={['move_clip', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'rate_stretch', 'slip', 'roll', 'split', 'delete', 'ripple_delete', 'ripple_delete_range', 'ripple_delete_ranges', 'lift_range', 'insert_time', 'close_gap', 'detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'split_at_shots', 'copy_pieces', 'switch_angle', 'switch_by_speaker']} />
67	
68	### Nests
69	
70	It can [nest clips](/editing/nests/) or take a nest apart. An edit lands in whichever timeline the window is showing, unless the Assistant names a nest, and it can [open a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/#open-a-nest) as you do. Markers belong to the timeline, never to a nest.
71	
72	<AtAGlance tools={['nest', 'unnest']} />
73	
74	### Speed
75	
76	It can [set a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), [reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/), [freeze a frame](/speed/freeze-frame/), add [speed ramps](/speed/make-a-ramp/), [retime a range](/speed/retime-range/) and [speed up the typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) in a screen recording.
77	
78	<AtAGlance tools={['set_speed', 'set_reversed', 'freeze_frame', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range', 'speed_up_typing']} />
79	
80	### Look and sound
81	
82	It can change how a clip looks and sounds: position, scale, crop, colour, filters, volume, fades, text and its style, and shapes. It can rename or label a clip, turn its picture or sound off, and [paste attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
83	
84	It can also work with [transitions](/motion/transitions/), [actions](/motion/actions/) and [zooms](/motion/zoom-to-region/), including [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), and with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/), [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) and [reframing](/framing/reframe-clip/).
85	
86	<AtAGlance tools={['set_video', 'set_audio', 'set_text', 'set_shape', 'set_clip', 'set_enabled', 'paste_attributes', 'analyze_cutout', 'add_transition', 'set_transition', 'set_transition_duration', 'set_transition_style', 'add_action', 'add_zoom_action', 'auto_zoom', 'switch_layout', 'reframe_clip', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']} />
87	
88	### Captions and words
89	
90	It can [import captions](/captions/import-captions/), [transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/), read a clip's or the whole timeline's timed words, [re-lay word captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) for the canvas, and [export captions](/captions/export-captions/).
91	
92	Transcribing runs on this Mac only, because the Assistant can't send audio to the cloud. Exporting captions asks first.
93	
94	<AtAGlance tools={['import_captions', 'transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'relay_captions', 'export_captions']} />
95	
96	### Audio clean-up
97	
98	It can find [silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [filler words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) and [cut them](#cut-words-by-asking), [normalise](/audio/normalize/) loudness, [enhance a voice](/audio/enhance-voice/), [match one clip's sound to another](/audio/match-audio/) and [synchronise audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
99	
100	<AtAGlance tools={['detect_silence', 'detect_fillers', 'normalize_clip', 'enhance_voice', 'match_audio', 'sync_audio']} />
101	
102	### Graphics
103	
104	It can write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics, import their fonts and pictures, and add [shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/). Exporting a graphic asks first. See [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/#the-assistant).
105	
106	<AtAGlance tools={['add_graphic_clip', 'set_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'get_graphic', 'graphic_reference', 'render_graphic', 'import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'delete_graphic', 'rename_graphic', 'restore_graphic', 'list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'export_graphic', 'import_graphic', 'add_shortcut_overlays']} />
107	
108	### Export
109	
110	It can [export](/export/export-sheet/), check how an export is going, or cancel it. Exporting asks first, because it writes a movie and replaces any file already there.
111	
112	<AtAGlance tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']} />
113	
114	## Cut words by asking
115	
116	You can ask the Assistant to take out filler words, silences or a false start, for example "cut the false start at the beginning of this clip." It cuts each request as one undo step, labelled **Undo Ripple Delete** rather than with the sheet's name.
117	
118	Its filler search reads only media that already has a cloud transcript made with filler words, and it can't upload audio to make one. In other media the search finds nothing, and it reports which media has no such transcript. To start the paid transcription, press **Transcribe** in the [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) sheet yourself.
119	
120	It removes a false start only when you ask, because deciding what counts as one is a judgement of meaning. It reads the words and their times, says which it will cut, then cuts them. The words come from a transcript the file already has or from this Mac's own speech recogniser, so no audio is uploaded. There's no menu command for this.
121	
122	See [Cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/).
123	
124	## It looks at rendered frames
125	
126	The Assistant checks its work by rendering a frame of the finished timeline, drawn the way an export draws it. It's told to look before and after a visual edit. It renders at the playhead unless it picks a time, and it's told to keep the image small.
127	
128	Rendering writes a picture file without asking. By default that's a temporary file.
129	
130	:::note
131	The frames it renders go to Anthropic, along with your messages and the project's details. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/).
132	:::
133	
134	Earlier renders don't survive compaction, so it renders again when it needs to look. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).
135	
136	## Each edit is an undo step
137	
138	Every edit the Assistant makes is its own undo step on the project, the same as your own, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names it after the edit. A turn isn't grouped, so a turn that made ten edits takes ten undos.
139	
140	Graphics files are the exception. Writing, restoring, deleting or importing a graphic, and importing a font or picture for one, change files in the project and make no undo step. See [Undo rules](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/#undo-rules).
141	
142	To take back its last change, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> outside the message field. You can also ask the Assistant to undo or redo.
143	
144	## How it behaves
145	
146	- **Short replies.** A reply is a sentence or two, and it doesn't repeat what the tool lines already show.
147	- **Captions only on request.** It writes or restyles a caption only when you ask.
148	- **Medium effort, thinking on.** The model always runs with these two Anthropic settings, and Frame Job's Settings has no control for them. The faint [working notes](/assistant/conversation/#working-notes) are its thinking updates.
149	
150	## Only its own window's project
151	
152	The Assistant acts only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation. A tool call that names another project doesn't run, and the transcript shows a `failed:` line: `The assistant edits its own window's project, …; … is a different project.`
153	
154	If its project has closed, a tool call fails with "The assistant's project is no longer open."
155	
156	## Limits
157	
158	- It works only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation.
159	- It needs your own Anthropic API key. There's no Frame Job account. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).
160	- It can't record the screen, close its window's project, or send audio to the cloud transcriber.
161	- A tool call that arrives during a drag waits until you release the mouse. See [While you are dragging](/assistant/stop-a-turn/#while-you-are-dragging).
162	- **Stop** doesn't cancel an export that's already been queued. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/).
163	- With [compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/) off, a long conversation eventually fails until you **Clear** it.
164	- Changing the key or the model ends every window's conversation.

2	title: "What it won't do and what it asks first"
3	description: The jobs the Assistant leaves to you, the file writes it asks about first, and how to answer or decline a question.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The Assistant can do most of what you can do in Frame Job, but a few jobs stay with you. It won't record, close its own project or send audio to the cloud, and it stops to ask before it exports, saves or copies media.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab, the row headed “The assistant asks first:”"
13	  tools={['record_screen', 'close_project', 'transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'export', 'export_captions', 'save_project', 'consolidate_media', 'export_graphic', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version']}
14	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
15	/>
16	
17	## Tools it will not call
18	
19	The Assistant works by calling tools, one for each job. Four jobs are yours to do yourself.
20	
21	| The job | Tool | Why | Do it with |
22	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
23	| Record the screen or a camera | `record_screen` | Recording needs a person at the Record button. | **File ▸ New Recording…** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) |
24	| Close the project | `close_project` | Closing the project would close the window the conversation lives in. | **File ▸ Close** (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>) |
25	| Transcribe in the cloud | `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine | Audio leaves your Mac only when you choose it, with the price in front of you. | **File ▸ Generate Captions…** |
26	| Transcribe for filler words | `transcribe_for_fillers` | The same: it uploads audio to the cloud. | **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** |
27	
28	`record_screen`, `close_project` and `transcribe_for_fillers` are taken out of what the Assistant can see, so it can't call them. `transcribe` stays, because transcribing on this Mac is allowed, and only a call that names the cloud engine is stopped.
29	
30	If one of the four is called anyway, it doesn't run. The transcript shows a [`failed:` line](/assistant/conversation/#failed-lines), "*tool* is not available to the assistant:" and the reason, which names the menu item to use instead. For the cloud engine the line starts `transcribe with engine "assemblyai"`.
31	
32	## Tools it asks about first
33	
34	Before it writes a movie, a caption file, a graphic package or the project, the Assistant waits for you.
35	
36	<Steps>
37	
38	1. The row headed "The assistant asks first:" appears in the Assistant tab, with a sentence saying what will happen, and **Allow** and **Deny** buttons. See [what each question reads](#what-each-question-reads).
39	
40	2. Read the sentence. A capitalised **REPLACES** means a file is already there.
41	
42	3. Click **Allow** to run the tool, or **Deny** to [decline](#declining).
43	
44	</Steps>
45	
46	Nothing runs until you click **Allow**. A question has no time limit, and it waits until you answer. You answer with a click only: no key answers it, and Return in the message box beeps. While a question waits, the **Send** button reads **Stop**.
47	
48	The transcript keeps a record of each answer, as `Allowed:` or `Declined:` and the sentence.
49	
50	## What each question reads
51	
52	Five tools always ask. The last two in this table ask only when the Assistant gives them a path to save to, because without one they don't write a project package.
53	
54	| Tool | The question reads |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| `export` | "export writes *path*", or "export REPLACES *path*" when a file is already there |
57	| `export_captions` | "export_captions writes *path*", or "export_captions REPLACES *path*" |
58	| `save_project` | "save_project writes *path*", or "save_project REPLACES *path*". With no path known, "save_project writes a file" |
59	| `consolidate_media` | "consolidate_media copies every referenced file into *package*/media", or "… into the project's package" when the project has never been saved |
60	| `export_graphic` | "export_graphic writes *path*", or "export_graphic REPLACES *path*", with `.fjgraphic` added when it's missing |
61	| `new_project_from_range` | "new_project_from_range writes *path*", with `.framejob` added when it's missing |
62	| `make_vertical_version` | "make_vertical_version writes *path*", with `.framejob` added when it's missing |
63	
64	A `~` in the path is expanded before the question is asked, so the sentence shows the full path.
65	
66	A few answers depend on what's on disk:
67	
68	- Saving a project that's already on disk reads "save_project REPLACES *path*", because the package is there. That's the normal question for an ordinary save.
69	- `new_project_from_range` and `make_vertical_version` never replace anything. With something already at the path the question reads REPLACES, but after **Allow** nothing is written, and the Assistant is told to choose a new path.
70	- A project that has never been saved needs a path. If `save_project` has none, the question reads "save_project writes a file" and nothing is written after **Allow**. `consolidate_media` also stops there, and the Assistant has to save the project first.
71	- For `export`, `export_captions` and `save_project`, the sentence shows the path as the Assistant wrote it. Frame Job adds or corrects the file extension as it writes, and REPLACES looks only at the path in the sentence, so a question that reads "writes" can still replace a file at the corrected name.
72	
73	## File writes that do not ask
74	
75	Some tools write files without a question.
76	
77	| What it does | Tools |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| Writes a rendered frame, a PNG unless another format is asked for, to a temporary file or to a path the Assistant names | `render_frame` |
80	| Writes a graphic's contact sheet as a PNG, to a temporary file or to a path the Assistant names | `render_graphic` |
81	| Writes modules, fonts and assets into the project's graphics folder | `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`, `import_graphic` |
82	| Saves a new, blank project at a path the Assistant names | `new_project` |
83	
84	`import_graphic` replaces nothing: a name that's already taken gets a suffix, and a picture whose name clashes stops the import.
85	
86	## The dot on the tab
87	
88	While a question waits, a small dot in the accent colour shows on the **Assistant** tab title, whichever inspector tab you're on. It sits to the right of the title, or raised at the title's top-right corner when the tab is narrow.
89	
90	The dot takes no clicks, so a click on it reaches the tab underneath. Frame Job doesn't switch tabs for you. If the inspector is hidden, **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) shows it and picks the tab.
91	
92	## Declining
93	
94	**Deny** tells the Assistant you declined. The tool doesn't run, and the Assistant is told not to try it again in the same [turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) unless you ask. The transcript shows a `failed:` line, "The person declined:" and the sentence, beside the `Declined:` record.
95	
96	A question also counts as declined when the turn or the conversation ends under it, and the transcript says what ended it:
97	
98	| What happened | The transcript reads |
99	| --- | --- |
100	| You clicked **Deny** | `Declined:` |
101	| You clicked [**Stop**](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) | `Declined (stop):` |
102	| A change of key or model in Settings ended the conversation | `Declined (close):` |
103	| The helper, the small program that talks to Anthropic, stopped | `Declined (helper):` |
104	
105	**Clear** and closing the window decline it too, and those take the transcript with them.
106	
107	## A waiting question holds only its window
108	
109	An unanswered question holds that window's Assistant and no other's. Other windows' Assistants and agents over MCP keep working while it waits, and you can go on editing.
110	
111	## MCP agents are not bound
112	
113	These rules belong to the Assistant. An agent connected over [MCP](/mcp/overview/) drives the same tools directly, so it's never asked first, and none of these tools is withheld from it.

2	title: "Stop a turn"
3	description: End what the Assistant is doing, see what stopping leaves in place, and how its tool calls wait for your drags and for each other.

5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A turn is everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply, including its tool calls, the actions it takes in Frame Job. You can end one at any moment with **Stop**. Nothing you or it has done is undone.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Stop, the Send button while a turn runs"
12	  tools={['transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'cancel_export']}
13	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
14	/>
15	
16	## Stop a turn
17	
18	Click **Stop**. It's the **Send** button, which reads **Stop** while a turn runs or a question waits.
19	
20	Stop is a click only. Pressing Return in the message box while a turn runs beeps, and it never stops the turn.
21	
22	When you click **Stop**, Frame Job:
23	
24	- ends the request to Anthropic
25	- [declines a question](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining) that's waiting, recorded as `Declined (stop):`
26	- cancels every tool call that hasn't started, and tells the Assistant "Cancelled by the user."
27	- ends a long-running job that has started, if it's one of those below
28	
29	Any other tool call that has already started is allowed to finish.
30	
31	| Running when you stop | What happens |
32	| --- | --- |
33	| Transcribing on this Mac | The transcription is cancelled. |
34	| Reading a clip's or the timeline's transcript | The read is cancelled, and nothing is saved from it. |
35	| Measuring loudness for Normalize, Enhance Voice or Match Audio | The measurement ends, and nothing changes. |
36	| Waiting for on-device analysis, to read it, split at shots, reframe a clip, make a vertical version, switch by speaker or analyse a cut-out | The wait ends, and nothing is made from it. |
37	
38	A timeline transcript that the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) also wants carries on. Stop withdraws only the Assistant's own request for it.
39	
40	## What stopping leaves in place
41	
42	Stop undoes nothing and ends only the turn.
43	
44	- Edits already made stay, and each one is still its own undo step.
45	- The conversation keeps the results of the tool calls that finished before you stopped, and your next message carries on from there.
46	- A stopped request shows no error.
47	- A response cut short is priced from what had arrived, as "at least $…". See [Responses cut short](/assistant/cost/#responses-cut-short).
48	- A stopped turn doesn't [compact](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) the conversation, even if it has passed the threshold.
49	
50	## Stop and exports
51	
52	An export is handed to the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) as soon as it starts, so Stop doesn't reach it. Cancel it in the Export Queue, or ask the Assistant to cancel it.
53	
54	## The 30-round limit
55	
56	One turn stops after 30 requests to Anthropic, which usually means 30 rounds of tool calls. No error appears at the limit. The turn ends with its `Cost:` line, whatever work was left. Send another message to carry on.
57	
58	## While you are dragging
59	
60	If one of the Assistant's tool calls arrives during a drag on the timeline, the canvas or an inspector slider, it waits until you release the mouse. It then runs as its own undo step, after yours, so your drag never undoes the Assistant's change or mixes with it.
61	
62	The call waits for as long as the mouse is held down, and a drag in any open project holds it. The same applies to agents over [MCP](/mcp/overview/).
63	
64	## Tool calls take turns
65	
66	The Assistant's tool calls and MCP agents' calls take turns, one at a time, and each window's calls run in order, so two of them never work on a project at the same moment. While a window waits for your **Allow** or **Deny**, MCP agents and other windows keep working.

2	title: "Long conversations"
3	description: Watch how much of the model's memory a conversation uses, and keep a long one going with compaction and tool result clearing.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A conversation with the Assistant grows with every message, tool result and rendered frame, and the model can only hold so much of it at once. That limit is its context window, measured in tokens, the small pieces of text a model counts in. The Context meter shows how full it is, and two settings keep a long conversation going.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
12	  keys="⌘,"
13	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Context"
14	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
15	/>
16	
17	## The context meter
18	
19	The **Context** row at the top of the Assistant tab shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response.
20	
21	| The row reads | When |
22	| --- | --- |
23	| "Nothing reported yet" | Before your first message in this window. |
24	| "12,000 of 200,000 tokens · 6%" | Once the model's window is known. The percentage shows at most one decimal. It can read "0 of …" for a moment after your first message, before the first response. |
25	| "12,000 tokens (window size unknown)" | Anthropic didn't report the window size. |
26	
27	When the inspector is narrow the figure shortens to "12,000 / 200,000 · 6%" or "6%", or to "12,000 tokens" with no known window. The tooltip always has the full figure.
28	
29	The bar under the figure fills in the accent colour and turns coral past 80%.
30	
31	**Clear** (↺), at the end of the row, puts the count back to zero, and so does a change of key or model, because each ends the conversation.
32	
33	## The settings
34	
35	Both settings are in **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**. A change applies without **Save** and keeps the conversation going. A new threshold counts from the end of the current turn, and a change to clearing applies from your next message.
36	
37	| Setting | What it does | Default | Range |
38	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
39	| **Compact when context reaches** … **tokens** | Replaces the conversation with a summary at the end of a turn. | On, 300,000 tokens | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens |
40	| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop older tool results from what the model sees. | Off | |
41	
42	The token field is dimmed while **Compact when context reaches** is off. A number outside the range beeps, and the field goes back to the stored value.
43	
44	## Compaction
45	
46	With **Compact when context reaches** on, the conversation is replaced by a summary at the end of the first turn that reaches the threshold. It never happens in the middle of a turn, and a [stopped](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) turn doesn't compact.
47	
48	The summary is asked to keep:
49	
50	- what you asked for and every preference you stated
51	- the project and any nest open
52	- the clips, tracks, markers and media involved
53	- the edits made, in order, and which were undone
54	- what's still open or was promised
55	
56	Rendered frames don't survive, so the summary describes in words what each one showed. The Assistant renders again when it needs to look.
57	
58	The transcript notes each step:
59	
60	| The transcript says | What it means |
61	| --- | --- |
62	| "Compacting the conversation (*N* tokens)…" | The summary has been asked for. |
63	| "Compacted: *N* → about *M* tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look." | It worked. The Context meter drops to about *M*. |
64	| "Compaction didn't finish (*reason*); it will try again after the next turn." | No summary came back. The conversation is unchanged. |
65	
66	The summary request is priced like any other response, and it's part of that turn's [`Cost:` line](/assistant/cost/#per-turn).
67	
68	:::tip
69	Compaction only starts once the conversation reaches the threshold, so the threshold has to be lower than the model's window. If the Context meter shows a window smaller than your threshold, lower it.
70	:::
71	
72	## With compaction off
73	
74	Nothing replaces the conversation, so it keeps growing until it fills the model's window. From then on each message fails, with an [error in the transcript](/assistant/conversation/#errors), until you click **Clear**. **Clear** ends the conversation, and nothing of it carries into the next message.
75	
76	## Clearing old tool results
77	
78	A tool result is what comes back from one of the Assistant's tool calls, and a project's details can run long. With **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** on, Anthropic may drop older ones from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens. It's a lighter step than compaction: the conversation stays, and only old tool results go.
79	
80	- It keeps the five most recent tool uses.
81	- It clears at least 50,000 tokens at a time.
82	- It can happen in the middle of a turn.
83	- It never clears tool search results, which are how the Assistant finds its tools.
84	
85	Each clearing adds a note to the transcript, "Cleared *N* old tool results (*M* tokens) from the model's view." The model may have to fetch something again afterwards.
86	
87	Each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write: Anthropic can't reuse its stored copy of the conversation, so it stores a new one, and that goes on your bill. That's why it clears in large pieces.
88	
89	## Related
90	
91	- [Read the conversation](/assistant/conversation/)
92	- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)
93	- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
94

1	---
2	title: "What it costs"
3	description: See what the Assistant costs per turn, per conversation and per month, and how far to trust the figures.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	The Assistant runs on your own Anthropic API key, so Anthropic bills you directly for what it uses. Frame Job shows you an estimate of that cost for each turn, each conversation and each month.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
12	  keys="⌘,"
13	  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Spend', 'The Cost line at the end of each turn']}
14	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
15	/>
16	
17	## Your own billing
18	
19	Every response is priced by Frame Job from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices, a public price table on GitHub. Every figure on this page is **Frame Job's own estimate**. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was actually billed.
20	
21	| Where | What it covers |
22	| --- | --- |
23	| The [`Cost:` line](#per-turn) in the transcript | One turn |
24	| The [**Spend** row](#per-conversation) in the tab | The conversation so far |
25	| The [month's line](#per-month) in Settings | The current calendar month, across every window |
26	
27	## Per turn
28	
29	Each turn ends with a line in the transcript. For example:
30	
31	`Cost: $0.0182 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-10-25)`
32	
33	The amount sums every response in the turn, the [compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) summary included. It shows to four decimal places, and a tiny positive amount reads "under $0.0001". A turn with no response has no `Cost:` line.
34	
35	The brackets name the price table and its date:
36	
37	| The brackets say | The prices came from |
38	| --- | --- |
39	| "bundled table of …" | The copy built into the app |
40	| "cached …" | The copy Frame Job keeps, from an earlier refresh |
41	| "fetched …" | A copy downloaded for this conversation |
42	
43	If a refresh failed, the brackets add "; not refreshed:" and the reason. A table that downloaded but couldn't be saved adds "; the price cache could not be written:" and the reason.
44	
45	## Unpriced responses
46	
47	A response that couldn't be priced shows as unknown with its reason, never as $0. In the `Cost:` line it reads "unknown (*reason*)", followed by "· at least $…" for the part that could be priced.
48	
49	A response goes unpriced when:
50	
51	- its model isn't in the price table, for example "*model* is not in the price table"
52	- the table lists the model but has no rate for what was used
53	- it used fast mode, for example `speed "fast" is not priced`
54	- it used a batch or priority tier
55	- it was a US-only request
56	
57	When a request sends more than 200,000 tokens, the model's higher rates apply if the table lists them.
58	
59	## Responses cut short
60	
61	A response cut short by [Stop](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) or an error is priced from what had arrived. It shows as "at least $… (a response was cut short)".
62	
63	## Per conversation
64	
65	The **Spend** row, under **Context** in the Assistant tab, adds up the conversation's turns since the last **Clear**, or since a key or model change ended the conversation.
66	
67	| The row reads | When |
68	| --- | --- |
69	| "Nothing yet" | Before the first response. |
70	| "$0.0532 · Frame Job's estimate" | Every response was priced. |
71	| "at least $… · Frame Job's estimate" | A response was cut short or couldn't be priced. Shortened to "≥$… · Frame Job's estimate" when the inspector is narrow. |
72	| "under $0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate" | A tiny positive amount. Shortened to `<$0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate` when narrow. |
73	| "unknown · Frame Job's estimate" | Nothing could be priced, or a response has no price and the priced part is under $0.00005. |
74	
75	Hovering the figure shows "What this conversation's responses cost at LiteLLM prices, as Frame Job estimates it. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."
76	
77	The figure is held in memory. If the helper, the small program that talks to Anthropic, stops, the row carries on from where it was.
78	
79	## Per month
80	
81	In **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**, a line under **Save** and **Remove** totals what the Assistant has cost in the current calendar month. The month runs in UTC, so it can turn over before or after midnight where you are.
82	
83	A response here is one reply from Anthropic, so one turn can count as several, and a compaction summary counts as one.
84	
85	| The line reads | When |
86	| --- | --- |
87	| "October 2026 (UTC): $1.24 over 87 responses." | Every response was priced. |
88	| "Nothing recorded in October 2026 (UTC)." | No responses this month. |
89	| "October 2026 (UTC): 5 responses; none could be priced." | No response had a price. |
90	| "October 2026 (UTC): 87 responses; 3 could not be priced, the rest came to $0.80." | Some had no price. They're counted, never added as $0. |
91	| "Reading the spend ledger…" | The [ledger](#the-spend-ledger) is being read. |
92	| "The spend ledger could not be read: *reason*." | It couldn't be read. |
93	| "This launch keeps no spend ledger." | Frame Job has no folder to keep one in. |
94	
95	Totals are rounded to the cent, and a positive amount that would round to $0.00 reads "under $0.01". When some lines of the ledger are damaged, the line adds a sentence such as "2 ledger lines could not be read." That count covers the whole ledger, because a line with no readable time can't be placed in a month.
96	
97	The line refreshes when Settings opens, and after each response while Settings is visible. During a refresh after a response, the last sentence stays until the new one is ready.
98	
99	Under it, a faint note says: "Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."
100	
101	## Prices refreshed daily
102	
103	Frame Job prices from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices. It has a table built into the app, and keeps a copy refreshed at most once a day at `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json`.
104	
105	A refresh is checked when a conversation starts, with a 30-second limit, and a turn keeps the prices it started with. The download is a plain request to `raw.githubusercontent.com`, made by the helper. It carries no key and no project data.
106	
107	If it fails, Frame Job prices from the cached copy or the built-in table, and the `Cost:` line says which it used.
108	
109	## The spend ledger
110	
111	The figures in Settings come from a ledger, `spend.jsonl` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. It's on your Mac, and only your account can read it.
112	
113	Each response is one line, with its time, the service, the model, the token counts, its speed and service tier, the prices used, and the dollars or why they're unknown. It never records your key or the conversation's content.
114	
115	If a response's cost can't be written, the transcript notes it once per conversation: "The spend ledger *path* could not be written: *reason*." That response is then missing from the month's total in Settings.
116	
117	## Related
118	
119	- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
120	- [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/)
121	- [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/)
122	- [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/)
123	- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
124

1	---
2	title: "Assistant privacy"
3	description: What goes to Anthropic when you use the Assistant, what stays on your Mac, and how long a conversation lasts.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	The Assistant works by sending your conversation to Anthropic, so it's worth knowing what that includes. Frame Job has no account or relay of its own: what you send goes to Anthropic under your own key, and nowhere else.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant tab', 'Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant ▸ ⓘ']}
12	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
13	/>
14	
15	## What goes to Anthropic
16	
17	When you use the Assistant, these go to Anthropic under your key:
18	
19	- **Your messages**, and a short block in front of each one: the project's name and path, the open nest, the playhead and the selection.
20	- **What the tools send back**: the project's details as JSON, including media file paths, any clip transcripts it reads, the reason when something couldn't be done, and other results.
21	- **The frames it renders** to look at the picture.
22	
23	What it costs is billed to your key. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
24	
25	Your key is handed straight to the helper, the small program Frame Job runs to talk to Anthropic. It isn't placed on a command line or in the helper's environment.
26	
27	When a conversation starts, the helper also asks Anthropic for the model's context window, under your key. That request names only the model.
28	
29	The Assistant [asks before](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-asks-about-first) it exports a movie or captions, saves the project or consolidates media. Other tools can still [write files without asking](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#file-writes-that-do-not-ask).
30	
31	## No audio to the cloud transcriber
32	
33	Audio never goes to the cloud transcriber from the Assistant. [Cloud transcription is withheld](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-will-not-call), so uploading audio stays your choice, in **File ▸ Generate Captions…** or **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**.
34	
35	## The price table download
36	
37	Once a day at most, the helper downloads LiteLLM's public price table from GitHub. That request carries no key and no project data. See [Prices refreshed daily](/assistant/cost/#prices-refreshed-daily).
38	
39	## What stays on your Mac
40	
41	Everything else stays on your Mac. The Assistant keeps these files in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`:
42	
43	| File | What it is |
44	| --- | --- |
45	| `anthropic-key` | Your key, in a file only you can read. |
46	| `spend.jsonl` | The [spend ledger](/assistant/cost/#the-spend-ledger). It holds token counts and dollars, never your key or the conversation's content. |
47	| `anthropic-prices.json` | The cached price table. |
48	
49	## The conversation lives in memory
50	
51	The conversation is kept in memory only, and goes when you clear it or close the window. Nothing of it is saved in the project or in the spend ledger.
52	
53	## Related
54	
55	- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
56	- [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/)
57	- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)
58	- [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/)
59	- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)
60

1	---
2	title: Set up the Assistant
3	description: Save your Anthropic API key, choose the model, and set how long conversations are kept in bounds.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	The Assistant runs on your own Anthropic API key. Save the key once in Settings and the Assistant tab is ready in every editor window.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
14	  keys="⌘,"
15	  where="Settings ▸ Assistant"
16	  needs="Your own Anthropic API key."
17	/>
18	
19	## Your own Anthropic key
20	
21	There's no Frame Job account and no relay in between. The Assistant talks to Anthropic with your key, and Anthropic bills what it uses to your account.
22	
23	Frame Job shows its own estimate of what each turn and each month costs. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). The Anthropic Console shows what you were actually billed.
24	
25	## Open Settings
26	
27	Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). **Assistant** is the second of the window's four sections, under **MCP** and above **Transcription**.
28	
29	<Shot
30	  name="02-settings.window"
31	  alt="The Settings window. The Assistant section has an Anthropic API key field reading Paste your key, a Model field showing claude-opus-5-5, Compact when context reaches ticked at 300,000 tokens, Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens unticked, the line No API key is set, Save and Remove buttons, and this month's spend. Transcription and Playback sit below it."
32	/>
33	
34	From top to bottom, the section holds:
35	
36	- the heading, with its [ⓘ](#what-the-info-button-says)
37	- **Anthropic API key:**
38	- [**Model:**](#choose-a-model)
39	- [**Compact when context reaches**](#compact-when-context-reaches)
40	- [**Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens**](#clear-old-tool-results)
41	- the [status line](#the-status-line), then **Save** and **Remove**
42	- this month's spend and a note on where the figure comes from. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
43	
44	## Save your key
45	
46	Create an API key in the Anthropic Console first. Settings has no link to your Anthropic account, so you'll need to go there yourself.
47	
48	<Steps>
49	
50	1. Paste your key into **Anthropic API key:**. With no key saved, the field reads "Paste your key".
51	
52	2. Click **Save**, or press <kbd>↩</kbd> in the field.
53	
54	</Steps>
55	
56	Spaces and line breaks around the key are dropped. The field empties, the status line reads "Key saved.", and the message field appears in every Assistant tab.
57	
58	A saved key is never shown again. The field shows a row of dots instead, and the row is always the same length, so it says nothing about your key. To change the key, paste the new one and save. It replaces the old one.
59	
60	**Save** with an empty field beeps and changes nothing.
61	
62	## No Verify
63	
64	AssemblyAI's key has a **Verify** button, but this one doesn't. Frame Job doesn't contact Anthropic until you send a message from the Assistant tab, so that's the test.
65	
66	A key Anthropic won't accept shows in the transcript straight away as `API error <status>: <message>`, with no retries.
67	
68	## Remove your key
69	
70	Click **Remove**. It's only enabled while a key is saved. The saved key is deleted and the status line reads "Key removed."
71	
72	Every window's message field gives way to the [no-key prompt](#the-no-key-prompt) straight away, unless [the environment](#a-key-from-the-environment) still supplies a key.
73	
74	## The status line
75	
76	A line above **Save** and **Remove** tells you the key's state and what your last press did.
77	
78	| The line says | What it means |
79	| --- | --- |
80	| "No API key is set." | There's no key in the field, saved or in the environment. This is a state, not an error, so it's in the ordinary muted colour. It goes as soon as you type in the field. |
81	| "Key saved." | **Save** worked. |
82	| "Key removed." | **Remove** worked. |
83	| "The API key could not be saved: …" | The key file couldn't be written or removed, and the line gives the reason in stronger text. |
84	
85	The last line appears for a failed **Remove** too, with the same opening words. A failed **Save** still empties the field, so paste the key again once you've fixed the cause. After a failed **Remove**, the saved key stays. Neither ends a conversation.
86	
87	## Choose a model
88	
89	Type a model id into **Model:**, or leave it blank for the default, `claude-opus-5-5`, which the field shows as its placeholder.
90	
91	There's no list to pick from, and Frame Job doesn't check what you type. An id Anthropic doesn't know shows up as an error in the transcript when you next send a message.
92	
93	The change counts when you press <kbd>↩</kbd> or leave the field. Changing to a different model [ends open conversations](#what-a-change-does).
94	
95	## Compact when context reaches
96	
97	Tokens are the units Anthropic counts text in, and a turn is everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply. When a turn ends with the conversation at or past this many tokens, the conversation is replaced by a summary. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/) for what that keeps and what it loses.
98	
99	| Setting | Default | Range |
100	| --- | --- | --- |
101	| The checkbox | On | Untick it to never compact |
102	| The token field | 300,000 | 20,000 to 900,000 |
103	
104	The field is enabled only while the box is ticked. A new number counts when you press <kbd>↩</kbd> or leave the field. Anything outside the range beeps, the field goes back to the stored number, and nothing is written.
105	
106	## Clear old tool results
107	
108	**Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** is off by default. Tick it and Anthropic drops old tool results from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens, even partway through a turn. Only the checkbox is yours to set. The 150,000 is fixed.
109	
110	The five most recent tool results always stay, tool search results are never cleared, and each clearing takes out at least 50,000 tokens. Each clearing also costs a fresh prompt-cache write: Anthropic stores the shortened conversation again and charges for that.
111	
112	## What a change does
113	
114	A conversation keeps the key and model it started with, so changing either has to end it.
115	
116	| You change | Open conversations | The note in the transcript |
117	| --- | --- | --- |
118	| The key, by saving or removing | End, in every window | "The API key changed; the next message starts a new conversation." |
119	| The model, to a different one | End, in every window | "The model is now …; the next message starts a new conversation." |
120	| Compaction or clearing | Carry on | None |
121	
122	When a conversation ends this way:
123	
124	- The transcript stays, and your next message starts a new conversation.
125	- The Spend row and the context meter start over.
126	- A running turn ends, and a question waiting for your answer is [declined](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining).
127	
128	A window with no conversation open has nothing to end, so it gets no note.
129	
130	**Save** always counts as a change, even if you paste the same key again. **Model:** doesn't: retyping the current model, or blanking the field while the default is in use, ends nothing.
131	
132	### Chat settings apply at once
133	
134	There's no Save button for the compaction and clearing settings. A change reaches every open conversation and keeps each one going. A new compaction threshold applies at the end of the current turn, and a change to clearing applies from the next message.
135	
136	## What the info button says
137	
138	The ⓘ beside the **Assistant** heading sums up the section:
139	
140	- The Assistant sends your messages, the project's details and the frames it renders to Anthropic, using your own key, and what it costs is billed to that key.
141	- It asks before writing a file. See [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/).
142	- The key is kept in a file only you can read, and it's never shown again once saved.
143	- Leave the model blank for `claude-opus-5-5`. Changing the key or the model starts a new conversation.
144	- Compaction replaces the conversation with a summary at the end of a turn past the threshold, which is 20,000 to 900,000 tokens and 300,000 by default. Earlier renders don't survive it.
145	- Clearing lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn, but never tool search results. Each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write.
146	- Changing either setting keeps the conversation.
147	
148	## Where the key is kept
149	
150	A saved key lives in a file named `anthropic-key` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`, beside AssemblyAI's key file. Only your user account can read it: the file's mode is `0600`, and Frame Job creates the folder at `0700` if it isn't there yet.
151	
152	The key goes to the Assistant's [helper](#if-the-helper-is-missing) when a conversation starts, on the helper's standard input, and nowhere else. It's never a tool argument, a launch argument or an answer to a tool. See [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) for the rest of that folder.
153	
154	## Out of reach of tools
155	
156	No tool reads or writes the key, the model or the chat settings. An agent connected over MCP can't see or change them, and neither can the Assistant.
157	
158	## A key from the environment
159	
160	With no saved key, Frame Job uses the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable, read from the environment Frame Job was started in. In practice this only applies when you launch Frame Job from a shell that sets the variable.
161	
162	- A saved key always comes first.
163	- An empty variable counts as no key.
164	- A key from the variable isn't saved, so **Remove** stays dimmed unless you've saved one too.
165	- With the variable set, removing a saved key leaves the message field in place, and the next conversation uses the variable's key.
166	
167	The same rule gives [AssemblyAI's key](/captions/assemblyai-key/) the variable `RC_ASSEMBLYAI_KEY`.
168	
169	## The no-key prompt
170	
171	Without a key, the Assistant tab still opens. In place of the message field it says "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and offers **Open Settings…**, which opens the Settings window. **View ▸ Assistant** stays enabled so the tab can tell you this.
172	
173	<Shot
174	  name="11b-assistant-tab.inspector"
175	  alt="The Assistant tab with no key set. Context reads Nothing reported yet, Spend reads Nothing yet, the transcript is empty, and at the foot is the line Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant, with an Open Settings button."
176	/>
177	
178	Saving the key brings the message field back at once.
179	
180	If the key goes some other way, say you delete the file by hand while Frame Job runs, the message field stays. An open conversation carries on with the key it started with. The next conversation fails to start, with "No Anthropic API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant."
181	
182	## If the helper is missing
183	
184	The Assistant runs in a small helper program inside the app, at `Contents/Helpers/framejob-agent`. Frame Job looks for it when a conversation starts. If it can't start one, a line appears in red in the transcript and your text stays in the message field. A helper that stops later says so in red too.
185	
186	| The transcript says | What it means |
187	| --- | --- |
188	| "The assistant helper is not in this build." | This copy of Frame Job has no helper it can run. [Install Frame Job again](/getting-started/requirements-and-install/). |
189	| "Could not start the assistant helper: …" | The helper is there but won't run, and the line gives the reason. |
190	| "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one." | The helper stopped during a conversation. See [Clear the conversation](/assistant/chat/#clear-the-conversation). |
191	
192	## Related
193	
194	- [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/)
195	- [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/)
196	- [What it costs](/assistant/cost/)
197	- [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/)
198	- [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/)
199	- [Settings](/reference/settings/)
200

1	---
2	title: Chat with the Assistant
3	description: Open the Assistant tab, ask for what you want in plain words, and manage the conversation that goes with each window.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The Assistant is a conversation with Claude, built into the inspector of every editor window. You ask in plain words, and it reads and edits that window's project.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
13	  keys="⌃⌘A"
14	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
15	  needs="Your own Anthropic API key. Without one, the tab says how to add it."
16	/>
17	
18	## The Assistant tab
19	
20	You might ask:
21	
22	- "trim the pauses out of the interview"
23	- "put a title over the first five seconds"
24	- "what is under the playhead?"
25	
26	The Assistant uses the same tools an agent uses over MCP, less a few held back from it, so its edits are ordinary edits. You watch each change land, and each one is its own undo step. See [What the Assistant can do](/assistant/what-it-can-do/).
27	
28	It's the fifth inspector tab, after **Clip**, **Media**, **Document** and **Transcript**. Before your first message, [save your key](/assistant/set-up/).
29	
30	## Open the Assistant
31	
32	Choose **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>). Frame Job shows the inspector if it was hidden, switches to the Assistant tab and puts the cursor in the message field.
33	
34	It isn't a toggle. Pressed while the tab is already showing, it only puts the cursor back in the field.
35	
36	The command stays enabled with no key, so the tab can [say what's needed](/assistant/set-up/#the-no-key-prompt). There's no message field to put the cursor in until then.
37	
38	## The tab's layout
39	
40	From top to bottom:
41	
42	| Part | What it shows |
43	| --- | --- |
44	| **Context** | How full the conversation is, with [**Clear**](#clear-the-conversation) (↺) at its right end. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/). |
45	| **Spend** | What this conversation has cost so far, as Frame Job estimates it. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). |
46	| The transcript | Your messages, the replies and each tool call. See [Read the conversation](/assistant/conversation/). |
47	| The ask-first row | Shows only while the Assistant is waiting for your permission. See [What it won't do and what it asks first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/). |
48	| The message field and **Send** | Where you type. |
49	
50	## The tab stays put
51	
52	The Assistant's own edits change the selection without moving you off the tab, so you can read along as it works.
53	
54	Clicking a clip in the timeline or on the canvas still switches to the **Clip** tab.
55	
56	## Send a message
57	
58	<Steps>
59	
60	1. Click in the message field, which reads "Ask about or edit this project…", and type what you want.
61	
62	2. Press <kbd>↩</kbd> or click **Send**.
63	
64	</Steps>
65	
66	The field empties once the message is taken, and the reply arrives in the transcript. Everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply is called a turn.
67	
68	The field starts one line high, grows to five lines as you type, and scrolls past that. Spaces and blank lines at either end are dropped, and a message of nothing else does nothing.
69	
70	You can type your next message while the Assistant works, but you can't send it until the turn ends.
71	
72	## Message field keys
73	
74	| Key | In the message field |
75	| --- | --- |
76	| <kbd>↩</kbd> or keypad Enter | Sends the message and gives the keys back to the editor, so <kbd>Space</kbd> plays while the Assistant works. While it's working or waiting for your answer, this beeps instead and the field keeps the keys. |
77	| <kbd>⇧↩</kbd>, <kbd>⌘↩</kbd>, <kbd>⌥↩</kbd> or <kbd>⌃↩</kbd> | Starts a new line |
78	| <kbd>Tab</kbd> or <kbd>⇧Tab</kbd> | Gives the keys back to the editor and never types a tab. With macOS Full Keyboard Access on, moves to the next or previous control. |
79	| <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> and <kbd>⇧⌘Z</kbd> | Undo and redo your typing |
80	
81	Clicking **Send** gives the keys back the same way <kbd>↩</kbd> does, and so does clicking anywhere else in the window below its title bar. See [Keys and typing](/getting-started/keys-and-typing/#start-and-finish-typing).
82	
83	Your typing never lands on the project's undo stack, and sending a message drops the field's own undo history. While the keys are in the field, <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> only undoes typing. Outside the field, it takes back the Assistant's last edit.
84	
85	<kbd>↩</kbd> never answers a question and never stops a turn. While an input method is composing, <kbd>↩</kbd> belongs to it.
86	
87	## If a message cannot be sent
88	
89	If the conversation can't start, the reason appears in red in the transcript and your text stays in the field. Your message isn't added to the transcript, so you can send it again once the cause is fixed.
90	
91	The usual causes are [a missing key](/assistant/set-up/#the-no-key-prompt) and [a helper that won't start](/assistant/set-up/#if-the-helper-is-missing).
92	
93	## Send becomes Stop
94	
95	The button reads **Send**, with the tooltip "Send the message". While a turn is running or waiting on you, it reads **Stop**, with the tooltip "Stop the turn".
96	
97	**Stop** is a click. It has no shortcut. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/).
98	
99	## What each message carries
100	
101	Each message starts with a short block describing your window at the moment you sent it, so "this clip" and "the selected titles" mean what you'd expect. The block holds:
102	
103	- the project's name, and its path, or a note that it's never been saved
104	- the nest open in the window, if there is one, or that the timeline is open
105	- the playhead's position
106	- the ids of the selected clips
107	
108	You don't see the block in the transcript, but it goes to Anthropic with your message. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/).
109	
110	It isn't updated during the turn. The Assistant is told to read the project again after its own edits.
111	
112	## One conversation per window
113	
114	Each editor window has its own conversation, about that window's project. Closing the window ends the conversation and [declines](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining) any question waiting for your answer.
115	
116	Conversations aren't saved with the project, so reopening it starts with an empty transcript.
117	
118	The Assistant can't close its own window. You do that with **File ▸ Close** (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>).
119	
120	## Clear the conversation
121	
122	Click **Clear** (↺, "Clear the conversation") at the right end of **Context**. It ends the conversation and empties the transcript, and your next message starts a fresh one.
123	
124	- **Spend** goes back to "Nothing yet".
125	- The context meter keeps the model's window size, so after a conversation it reads "0 of … tokens · 0%", with that size in place of the dots, until the next response.
126	- Clear asks for no confirmation. It ends a running turn and declines a waiting question.
127	
128	The project is untouched. Edits already made stay, each still its own undo step.
129

3	description: "Follow what the Assistant is doing as it works: its replies, its tool calls, the questions it asked, and why it stopped."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	The transcript in the Assistant tab shows everything that happens in a conversation: your messages, the replies, each tool call, each question, and what went wrong. Reading it tells you what the Assistant did and why it stopped.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
12	  keys="⌃⌘A"
13	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
14	  needs="Your own Anthropic API key"
15	/>
16	
17	## What's in the transcript
18	
19	| You see | It looks like |
20	| --- | --- |
21	| Your message | Semibold |
22	| The Assistant's [replies](#replies) | Regular |
23	| Its [working notes](#working-notes) | Small and faint |
24	| [Tool call lines](#tool-call-lines), [`failed:` lines](#failed-lines), [permission lines](#permission-lines) and [notes](#notes) | Small monospace |
25	| [Errors](#errors) | Red |
26	
27	## Replies
28	
29	A reply streams in as it's written, under your message. The transcript scrolls to the newest line each time anything arrives, even if you've scrolled up to read something earlier.
30	
31	Replies are short on purpose. See [How it behaves](/assistant/what-it-can-do/#how-it-behaves).
32	
33	## Working notes
34	
35	Between tool calls the Assistant writes small, faint notes on what it's working through. They're its thinking updates, and they stream in as replies do. They aren't addressed to you, and there's nothing to answer.
36	
37	## Tool call lines
38	
39	A tool is one action the Assistant can take in Frame Job, such as splitting a clip. Each tool call is one line, with the tool's name and its arguments, the details it was given:
40	
41	```
42	split (at: 1200000, clips: [12])
43	```
44	
45	That line splits clip 12 at the timeline's two-second mark. A time shows as a large number, 600,000 to the second.
46	
47	Arguments are in alphabetical order, and the line shows only their first 70 characters. A call with no arguments shows the tool's name alone.
48	
49	The line appears when the call starts. Apart from a [permission line](#permission-lines) if it asked you first, a call that works adds nothing more to the transcript, and you see its result in the project. A call that doesn't work adds a [`failed:` line](#failed-lines). [All tools](/mcp/tools/) describes every tool.
50	
51	## `failed:` lines
52	
53	A tool call that didn't work is followed by `failed:` and the reason. The line shows the first 200 characters of what the tool said.
54	
55	The Assistant reads the same message in full, so it can correct itself. A `failed:` line followed by another tool call is normal, and often the next try works.
56	
57	| The line reads | What happened |
58	| --- | --- |
59	| `failed: … was refused at …: …` | Frame Job wouldn't make the edit. The line names the edit, then gives the same sentence you'd see yourself. See [When an edit is refused](/getting-started/refused-edits/). |
60	| `failed: … made no change: the project is already in that state.` | The edit wouldn't have changed anything. |
61	| `failed: The person declined: …` | You chose **Deny**, or the question was declined for you. The Assistant won't try that call again this turn unless you ask. |
62	| `failed: Cancelled by the user.` | **Stop** cancelled the call before it started. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/). |
63	| `failed: … is not available to the assistant: …` | The Assistant isn't allowed that tool. The reason names the menu item to use instead. See [What it won't do](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/). |
64	
65	## Permission lines
66	
67	The Assistant [asks before it writes a file](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/). Once a question is answered, the transcript records the outcome with the question's sentence, for example `Allowed: export writes /Volumes/Work/cut.mp4`.
68	
69	| The line starts | What happened |
70	| --- | --- |
71	| `Allowed:` | You chose **Allow**. |
72	| `Declined:` | You chose **Deny**. |
73	| `Declined (stop):` | You chose **Stop** while the question was waiting. |
74	| `Declined (close):` | The conversation ended while the question was waiting, for example because the key or the model changed. |
75	| `Declined (helper):` | [The helper stopped](#if-the-helper-stops) while the question was waiting. |
76	
77	## Notes
78	
79	Frame Job writes its own small monospace notes into the transcript.
80	
81	| The note reads | What it means |
82	| --- | --- |
83	| `Cost: …` | What the turn came to, at the end of each turn. For example, `Cost: $0.0312 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-11-02)`. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/). |
84	| `Compacting the conversation (… tokens)…` | The conversation has reached your compaction threshold, and Frame Job is replacing it with a summary. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/). |
85	| `Compacted: … → about … tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look.` | The summary is in place. |
86	| `Compaction didn't finish (…); it will try again after the next turn.` | No summary came back, so the conversation is unchanged. |
87	| `Cleared … old tool results (… tokens) from the model's view.` | Old results were dropped from what the model sees. This only happens with clearing turned on in Settings. |
88	| `The model is now …; the next message starts a new conversation.` | The model changed in Settings. |
89	| `The API key changed; the next message starts a new conversation.` | The key was saved or removed in Settings. |
90	| `The spend ledger … could not be written: ….` | A response's cost couldn't be recorded. The note appears once per conversation, and an unrecorded response is missing from the month's total in Settings. |
91	
92	## Errors
93	
94	An error is a red line, and it says what went wrong.
95	
96	| The error reads | What it means |
97	| --- | --- |
98	| `API error status: message` | Anthropic turned the request down or it failed, for example a bad key, a rate limit or an outage. The status is Anthropic's, and it's blank when the request never reached Anthropic. |
99	| "The reply was cut off at the output limit." | The response reached 32,000 [tokens](/assistant/context-and-compaction/), the small pieces of text a model counts in. Thinking counts toward that as well as the reply. |
100	| "The model declined this request." | The model wouldn't do what you asked. |
101	| "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one." | See [If the helper stops](#if-the-helper-stops). |
102	
103	If a conversation can't start, for example because the helper won't run, the reason shows as an error and your message stays in the field.
104	
105	A request you end with **Stop** shows no error.
106	
107	## Automatic retries
108	
109	Rate limits, outages and connection failures are retried up to three times before an error appears. Nothing shows in the transcript during a retry, so a turn can seem to pause. A bad key fails at once.
110	
111	## Select and copy
112	
113	The transcript is one block of text, so you can drag a selection across entries. <kbd>⌘C</kbd> copies it as plain text, with a line break between entries.
114	
115	A conversation isn't saved with the project. Copy anything you want to keep before you close the window.
116	
117	## If the helper stops
118	
119	The helper is the background program that talks to Anthropic for the Assistant. If it stops:
120	
121	- The transcript says "The assistant helper stopped. Clear the conversation to start a new one."
122	- A question that was waiting is declined, with a `Declined (helper):` line.
123	- The edits the Assistant already made stay in the project.
124	
125	Your next message starts a new conversation under the old transcript. The Assistant doesn't remember anything from before, and the Spend row carries on from where it was. To start clean, choose **Clear** (↺) at the top of the tab.
126	
127	## Good to know
128	
129	- A [turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/), everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply, takes at most 30 rounds of tool calls. At that point it ends with no error line, and your next message carries on from there.
130	- Each window has its own transcript. **Clear** empties it, and closing the window ends it. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/).

8	The Assistant edits the project in its own window. You ask in plain words, it makes the edits one at a time, and each one lands where you can see it. Almost all of them [can be undone](#each-edit-is-an-undo-step). This page goes through what you can ask for, job by job, and where the limits are.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="View ▸ Assistant"
12	  keys="⌃⌘A"
13	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab"
14	  tools={['get_project', 'render_frame', 'undo', 'redo']}
15	  needs="Your own Anthropic API key"
16	/>
17	
18	## The same tools as MCP
19	
20	The Assistant works by calling tools, one for each job. They're the same tools an outside AI agent uses when it connects to Frame Job [over MCP](/mcp/overview/), so anything here is something an agent can do too. There are a few exceptions, listed in [What it won't do](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/), and some tools that write files [ask you first](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-asks-about-first).
21	
22	Four tools are always at hand: reading the project, rendering a frame, undo and redo. It finds every other tool by searching for what it wants to do, so you never need to name one. A tool kept from it outright doesn't turn up in that search at all.
23	
24	Each job below lists its tools, because those are the names you'll see in the [tool call lines](/assistant/conversation/#tool-call-lines). [All tools](/mcp/tools/) describes each one.
25	
26	## What you can ask for
27	
28	Ask in your own words, for example "put a title over the first five seconds". You don't need to know which job a request falls under. See [Chat with the Assistant](/assistant/chat/) for how to send one.
29	
30	### Projects and navigation
31	
32	It can open, create and save projects, move the playhead, set the in and out range, change the selection, and enter or leave a nest. It can also make a [new project from a range](/projects/new-project-from-range/) or a [vertical version](/framing/make-vertical-version/).
33	
34	Saving asks first. Making a new project from a range or a vertical version asks first when it names where to save. Moving the playhead, setting the range and changing the selection aren't edits, so they make no undo step.
35	
36	A project it opens or creates gets a window of its own, and the Assistant stays with the project it started in.
37	
38	<AtAGlance tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version', 'save_project', 'set_playhead', 'set_range', 'set_selection', 'set_scope']} />
39	
40	### Tracks, markers and the canvas
41	
42	It can add, remove and reorder tracks, remove the empty ones, rename a track, hide, mute, solo or lock one, and set its [matte](/canvas/matte-tracks/) and [mix](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/). It can add, move, rename and remove [markers](/timeline/markers/), make one a chapter, and set its colour, which you can't do yourself. It can change the canvas's [size](/projects/canvas-size/), [frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) and [background](/projects/background-and-timecode/).
43	
44	<AtAGlance tools={['add_track', 'remove_track', 'move_track', 'set_track', 'remove_empty_tracks', 'add_marker', 'set_marker', 'remove_marker', 'set_canvas']} />
45	
46	### Media
47	
48	It can [import](/projects/import-media/), [relink](/projects/relink-media/) and [remove](/projects/remove-media/) media, [copy it into the project](/projects/consolidate-media/) and set a file's [camera log](/hdr/camera-log/). Copying into the project asks first.
49	
50	It can also save where a file's speech is, read the [on-device analysis](/projects/media-analysis/) of a file, and attach or read a recording's [cursor file](/recording/cursor-files/).
51	
52	<AtAGlance tools={['import_media', 'add_media', 'relink_media', 'remove_media', 'set_media_color', 'set_media_speech', 'consolidate_media', 'get_media_analysis', 'set_media_cursor', 'get_cursor_events']} />
53	
54	### Placing clips
55	
56	It can place media, [text](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/), [shapes](/text-and-shapes/shape-clips/), [backgrounds](/canvas/backgrounds/), [adjustment clips](/color/adjustment-clips/) and [graphics](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/). It can [insert and overwrite](/editing/insert-and-overwrite/), paste and duplicate, and put [text behind a subject](/effects/text-behind-subject/).

60	### Editing clips
61	
62	It can [move](/editing/move-clips/), [trim](/editing/trimming/), [split](/editing/splitting/), [slip and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/), [rate-stretch](/speed/rate-stretch/), [ripple-delete and lift](/editing/delete-clips/), [insert time and close gaps](/editing/close-gaps/). It can [detach audio and attach it again](/audio/detach-and-attach/) and make [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
63	
64	For several cameras or long recordings it can [split at shot changes](/editing/split-at-shot-changes/), [copy pieces to another track](/multicam/copy-pieces/), [switch a shot's angle](/multicam/switch-angle/) and [switch by speaker](/multicam/switch-by-speaker/).

67	
68	### Nests
69	
70	It can [nest clips](/editing/nests/) or take a nest apart. An edit lands in whichever timeline the window is showing, unless the Assistant names a nest, and it can [open a nest](/editing/inside-a-nest/#open-a-nest) as you do. Markers belong to the timeline, never to a nest.
