72	<AtAGlance tools={['nest', 'unnest']} />
73	
74	### Speed
75	
76	It can [set a clip's speed](/speed/change-speed/), [reverse a clip](/speed/reverse/), [freeze a frame](/speed/freeze-frame/), add [speed ramps](/speed/make-a-ramp/), [retime a range](/speed/retime-range/) and [speed up the typing](/recording/speed-up-typing/) in a screen recording.
77	
78	<AtAGlance tools={['set_speed', 'set_reversed', 'freeze_frame', 'add_speed_ramp', 'retime_range', 'speed_up_typing']} />
79	
80	### Look and sound
81	
82	It can change how a clip looks and sounds: position, scale, crop, colour, filters, volume, fades, text and its style, and shapes. It can rename or label a clip, turn its picture or sound off, and [paste attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).
83	
84	It can also work with [transitions](/motion/transitions/), [actions](/motion/actions/) and [zooms](/motion/zoom-to-region/), including [Auto Zoom](/recording/auto-zoom/), and with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/), [camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) and [reframing](/framing/reframe-clip/).
85	
86	<AtAGlance tools={['set_video', 'set_audio', 'set_text', 'set_shape', 'set_clip', 'set_enabled', 'paste_attributes', 'analyze_cutout', 'add_transition', 'set_transition', 'set_transition_duration', 'set_transition_style', 'add_action', 'add_zoom_action', 'auto_zoom', 'switch_layout', 'reframe_clip', 'set_action', 'set_action_end', 'remove_action']} />
87	
88	### Captions and words
89	
90	It can [import captions](/captions/import-captions/), [transcribe on this Mac](/captions/on-device-transcription/), read a clip's or the whole timeline's timed words, [re-lay word captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) for the canvas, and [export captions](/captions/export-captions/).
91	
92	Transcribing runs on this Mac only, because the Assistant can't send audio to the cloud. Exporting captions asks first.
93	
94	<AtAGlance tools={['import_captions', 'transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'relay_captions', 'export_captions']} />
95	
96	### Audio clean-up
97	
98	It can find [silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) and [filler words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) and [cut them](#cut-words-by-asking), [normalise](/audio/normalize/) loudness, [enhance a voice](/audio/enhance-voice/), [match one clip's sound to another](/audio/match-audio/) and [synchronise audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/).
99	
100	<AtAGlance tools={['detect_silence', 'detect_fillers', 'normalize_clip', 'enhance_voice', 'match_audio', 'sync_audio']} />
101	
102	### Graphics
103	
104	It can write, change, place, render, rename, delete, restore, export and import graphics, import their fonts and pictures, and add [shortcut overlays](/recording/shortcut-overlays/). Exporting a graphic asks first. See [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/#the-assistant).
105	
106	<AtAGlance tools={['add_graphic_clip', 'set_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'get_graphic', 'graphic_reference', 'render_graphic', 'import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'delete_graphic', 'rename_graphic', 'restore_graphic', 'list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'export_graphic', 'import_graphic', 'add_shortcut_overlays']} />
107	
108	### Export
109	
110	It can [export](/export/export-sheet/), check how an export is going, or cancel it. Exporting asks first, because it writes a movie and replaces any file already there.
111	
112	<AtAGlance tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']} />
113	
114	## Cut words by asking
115	
116	You can ask the Assistant to take out filler words, silences or a false start, for example "cut the false start at the beginning of this clip." It cuts each request as one undo step, labelled **Undo Ripple Delete** rather than with the sheet's name.
117	
118	Its filler search reads only media that already has a cloud transcript made with filler words, and it can't upload audio to make one. In other media the search finds nothing, and it reports which media has no such transcript. To start the paid transcription, press **Transcribe** in the [Remove Filler Words](/cleanup/remove-filler-words/) sheet yourself.
119	
120	It removes a false start only when you ask, because deciding what counts as one is a judgement of meaning. It reads the words and their times, says which it will cut, then cuts them. The words come from a transcript the file already has or from this Mac's own speech recogniser, so no audio is uploaded. There's no menu command for this.
121	
122	See [Cut false starts](/cleanup/false-starts/).
123	
124	## It looks at rendered frames
125	
126	The Assistant checks its work by rendering a frame of the finished timeline, drawn the way an export draws it. It's told to look before and after a visual edit. It renders at the playhead unless it picks a time, and it's told to keep the image small.
127	
128	Rendering writes a picture file without asking. By default that's a temporary file.
129	
130	:::note
131	The frames it renders go to Anthropic, along with your messages and the project's details. See [Assistant privacy](/assistant/privacy/).
132	:::
133	
134	Earlier renders don't survive compaction, so it renders again when it needs to look. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).
135	
136	## Each edit is an undo step
137	
138	Every edit the Assistant makes is its own undo step on the project, the same as your own, and **Edit ▸ Undo** names it after the edit. A turn isn't grouped, so a turn that made ten edits takes ten undos.
139	
140	Graphics files are the exception. Writing, restoring, deleting or importing a graphic, and importing a font or picture for one, change files in the project and make no undo step. See [Undo rules](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/#undo-rules).
141	
142	To take back its last change, press <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> outside the message field. You can also ask the Assistant to undo or redo.
143	
144	## How it behaves
145	
146	- **Short replies.** A reply is a sentence or two, and it doesn't repeat what the tool lines already show.
147	- **Captions only on request.** It writes or restyles a caption only when you ask.
148	- **Medium effort, thinking on.** The model always runs with these two Anthropic settings, and Frame Job's Settings has no control for them. The faint [working notes](/assistant/conversation/#working-notes) are its thinking updates.
149	
150	## Only its own window's project
151	
152	The Assistant acts only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation. A tool call that names another project doesn't run, and the transcript shows a `failed:` line: `The assistant edits its own window's project, …; … is a different project.`
153	
154	If its project has closed, a tool call fails with "The assistant's project is no longer open."
155	
156	## Limits
157	
158	- It works only on the project in its own window, and each window has its own conversation.
159	- It needs your own Anthropic API key. There's no Frame Job account. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).
160	- It can't record the screen, close its window's project, or send audio to the cloud transcriber.
161	- A tool call that arrives during a drag waits until you release the mouse. See [While you are dragging](/assistant/stop-a-turn/#while-you-are-dragging).
162	- **Stop** doesn't cancel an export that's already been queued. See [Stop a turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/).
163	- With [compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/) off, a long conversation eventually fails until you **Clear** it.
164	- Changing the key or the model ends every window's conversation.
165

2	title: "What it won't do and what it asks first"
3	description: The jobs the Assistant leaves to you, the file writes it asks about first, and how to answer or decline a question.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The Assistant can do most of what you can do in Frame Job, but a few jobs stay with you. It won't record, close its own project or send audio to the cloud, and it stops to ask before it exports, saves or copies media.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab, the row headed “The assistant asks first:”"
13	  tools={['record_screen', 'close_project', 'transcribe', 'transcribe_for_fillers', 'export', 'export_captions', 'save_project', 'consolidate_media', 'export_graphic', 'new_project_from_range', 'make_vertical_version']}
14	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
15	/>
16	
17	## Tools it will not call
18	
19	The Assistant works by calling tools, one for each job. Four jobs are yours to do yourself.
20	
21	| The job | Tool | Why | Do it with |
22	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
23	| Record the screen or a camera | `record_screen` | Recording needs a person at the Record button. | **File ▸ New Recording…** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) |
24	| Close the project | `close_project` | Closing the project would close the window the conversation lives in. | **File ▸ Close** (<kbd>⌘W</kbd>) |
25	| Transcribe in the cloud | `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine | Audio leaves your Mac only when you choose it, with the price in front of you. | **File ▸ Generate Captions…** |
26	| Transcribe for filler words | `transcribe_for_fillers` | The same: it uploads audio to the cloud. | **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** |
27	
28	`record_screen`, `close_project` and `transcribe_for_fillers` are taken out of what the Assistant can see, so it can't call them. `transcribe` stays, because transcribing on this Mac is allowed, and only a call that names the cloud engine is stopped.
29	
30	If one of the four is called anyway, it doesn't run. The transcript shows a [`failed:` line](/assistant/conversation/#failed-lines), "*tool* is not available to the assistant:" and the reason, which names the menu item to use instead. For the cloud engine the line starts `transcribe with engine "assemblyai"`.
31	
32	## Tools it asks about first
33	
34	Before it writes a movie, a caption file, a graphic package or the project, the Assistant waits for you.
35	
36	<Steps>
37	
38	1. The row headed "The assistant asks first:" appears in the Assistant tab, with a sentence saying what will happen, and **Allow** and **Deny** buttons. See [what each question reads](#what-each-question-reads).
39	
40	2. Read the sentence. A capitalised **REPLACES** means a file is already there.
41	
42	3. Click **Allow** to run the tool, or **Deny** to [decline](#declining).
43	
44	</Steps>
45	
46	Nothing runs until you click **Allow**. A question has no time limit, and it waits until you answer. You answer with a click only: no key answers it, and Return in the message box beeps. While a question waits, the **Send** button reads **Stop**.
47	
48	The transcript keeps a record of each answer, as `Allowed:` or `Declined:` and the sentence.
49	
50	## What each question reads
51	
52	Five tools always ask. The last two in this table ask only when the Assistant gives them a path to save to, because without one they don't write a project package.
53	
54	| Tool | The question reads |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| `export` | "export writes *path*", or "export REPLACES *path*" when a file is already there |
57	| `export_captions` | "export_captions writes *path*", or "export_captions REPLACES *path*" |
58	| `save_project` | "save_project writes *path*", or "save_project REPLACES *path*". With no path known, "save_project writes a file" |
59	| `consolidate_media` | "consolidate_media copies every referenced file into *package*/media", or "… into the project's package" when the project has never been saved |
60	| `export_graphic` | "export_graphic writes *path*", or "export_graphic REPLACES *path*", with `.fjgraphic` added when it's missing |
61	| `new_project_from_range` | "new_project_from_range writes *path*", with `.framejob` added when it's missing |
62	| `make_vertical_version` | "make_vertical_version writes *path*", with `.framejob` added when it's missing |
63	
64	A `~` in the path is expanded before the question is asked, so the sentence shows the full path.
65	
66	A few answers depend on what's on disk:
67	
68	- Saving a project that's already on disk reads "save_project REPLACES *path*", because the package is there. That's the normal question for an ordinary save.
69	- `new_project_from_range` and `make_vertical_version` never replace anything. With something already at the path the question reads REPLACES, but after **Allow** nothing is written, and the Assistant is told to choose a new path.
70	- A project that has never been saved needs a path. If `save_project` has none, the question reads "save_project writes a file" and nothing is written after **Allow**. `consolidate_media` also stops there, and the Assistant has to save the project first.
71	- For `export`, `export_captions` and `save_project`, the sentence shows the path as the Assistant wrote it. Frame Job adds or corrects the file extension as it writes, and REPLACES looks only at the path in the sentence, so a question that reads "writes" can still replace a file at the corrected name.
72	
73	## File writes that do not ask
74	
75	Some tools write files without a question.
76	
77	| What it does | Tools |
78	| --- | --- |
79	| Writes a rendered frame, a PNG unless another format is asked for, to a temporary file or to a path the Assistant names | `render_frame` |
80	| Writes a graphic's contact sheet as a PNG, to a temporary file or to a path the Assistant names | `render_graphic` |
81	| Writes modules, fonts and assets into the project's graphics folder | `write_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`, `import_graphic_asset`, `import_graphic` |
82	| Saves a new, blank project at a path the Assistant names | `new_project` |
83	
84	`import_graphic` replaces nothing: a name that's already taken gets a suffix, and a picture whose name clashes stops the import.
85	
86	## The dot on the tab
87	
88	While a question waits, a small dot in the accent colour shows on the **Assistant** tab title, whichever inspector tab you're on. It sits to the right of the title, or raised at the title's top-right corner when the tab is narrow.
89	
90	The dot takes no clicks, so a click on it reaches the tab underneath. Frame Job doesn't switch tabs for you. If the inspector is hidden, **View ▸ Assistant** (<kbd>⌃⌘A</kbd>) shows it and picks the tab.
91	
92	## Declining
93	
94	**Deny** tells the Assistant you declined. The tool doesn't run, and the Assistant is told not to try it again in the same [turn](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) unless you ask. The transcript shows a `failed:` line, "The person declined:" and the sentence, beside the `Declined:` record.
95	
96	A question also counts as declined when the turn or the conversation ends under it, and the transcript says what ended it:
97	
98	| What happened | The transcript reads |
99	| --- | --- |
100	| You clicked **Deny** | `Declined:` |
101	| You clicked [**Stop**](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) | `Declined (stop):` |
102	| A change of key or model in Settings ended the conversation | `Declined (close):` |
103	| The helper, the small program that talks to Anthropic, stopped | `Declined (helper):` |
104	
105	**Clear** and closing the window decline it too, and those take the transcript with them.
106	
107	## A waiting question holds only its window
108	
109	An unanswered question holds that window's Assistant and no other's. Other windows' Assistants and agents over MCP keep working while it waits, and you can go on editing.
110	
111	## MCP agents are not bound
112	
113	These rules belong to the Assistant. An agent connected over [MCP](/mcp/overview/) drives the same tools directly, so it's never asked first, and none of these tools is withheld from it.

2	title: "Stop a turn"
3	description: End what the Assistant is doing, see what stopping leaves in place, and how its tool calls wait for your drags and for each other.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A turn is everything the Assistant does between your message and the end of its reply, including its tool calls, the actions it takes in Frame Job. You can end one at any moment with **Stop**. Nothing you or it has done is undone.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Stop, the Send button while a turn runs"
12	  tools={['transcribe', 'get_transcript', 'get_timeline_transcript', 'cancel_export']}
13	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
14	/>
15	
16	## Stop a turn
17	
18	Click **Stop**. It's the **Send** button, which reads **Stop** while a turn runs or a question waits.
19	
20	Stop is a click only. Pressing Return in the message box while a turn runs beeps, and it never stops the turn.
21	
22	When you click **Stop**, Frame Job:
23	
24	- ends the request to Anthropic
25	- [declines a question](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#declining) that's waiting, recorded as `Declined (stop):`
26	- cancels every tool call that hasn't started, and tells the Assistant "Cancelled by the user."
27	- ends a long-running job that has started, if it's one of those below
28	
29	Any other tool call that has already started is allowed to finish.
30	
31	| Running when you stop | What happens |
32	| --- | --- |
33	| Transcribing on this Mac | The transcription is cancelled. |
34	| Reading a clip's or the timeline's transcript | The read is cancelled, and nothing is saved from it. |
35	| Measuring loudness for Normalize, Enhance Voice or Match Audio | The measurement ends, and nothing changes. |
36	| Waiting for on-device analysis, to read it, split at shots, reframe a clip, make a vertical version, switch by speaker or analyse a cut-out | The wait ends, and nothing is made from it. |
37	
38	A timeline transcript that the [Transcript tab](/captions/transcript-tab/) also wants carries on. Stop withdraws only the Assistant's own request for it.
39	
40	## What stopping leaves in place
41	
42	Stop undoes nothing and ends only the turn.
43	
44	- Edits already made stay, and each one is still its own undo step.
45	- The conversation keeps the results of the tool calls that finished before you stopped, and your next message carries on from there.
46	- A stopped request shows no error.
47	- A response cut short is priced from what had arrived, as "at least $…". See [Responses cut short](/assistant/cost/#responses-cut-short).
48	- A stopped turn doesn't [compact](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) the conversation, even if it has passed the threshold.
49	
50	## Stop and exports
51	
52	An export is handed to the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/) as soon as it starts, so Stop doesn't reach it. Cancel it in the Export Queue, or ask the Assistant to cancel it.
53	
54	## The 30-round limit
55	
56	One turn stops after 30 requests to Anthropic, which usually means 30 rounds of tool calls. No error appears at the limit. The turn ends with its `Cost:` line, whatever work was left. Send another message to carry on.
57	
58	## While you are dragging
59	
60	If one of the Assistant's tool calls arrives during a drag on the timeline, the canvas or an inspector slider, it waits until you release the mouse. It then runs as its own undo step, after yours, so your drag never undoes the Assistant's change or mixes with it.
61	
62	The call waits for as long as the mouse is held down, and a drag in any open project holds it. The same applies to agents over [MCP](/mcp/overview/).
63	
64	## Tool calls take turns
65	
66	The Assistant's tool calls and MCP agents' calls take turns, one at a time, and each window's calls run in order, so two of them never work on a project at the same moment. While a window waits for your **Allow** or **Deny**, MCP agents and other windows keep working.
67

2	title: "Long conversations"
3	description: Watch how much of the model's memory a conversation uses, and keep a long one going with compaction and tool result clearing.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A conversation with the Assistant grows with every message, tool result and rendered frame, and the model can only hold so much of it at once. That limit is its context window, measured in tokens, the small pieces of text a model counts in. The Context meter shows how full it is, and two settings keep a long conversation going.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
12	  keys="⌘,"
13	  where="Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Context"
14	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
15	/>
16	
17	## The context meter
18	
19	The **Context** row at the top of the Assistant tab shows how much of the model's context window the conversation is using, as of the last response.
20	
21	| The row reads | When |
22	| --- | --- |
23	| "Nothing reported yet" | Before your first message in this window. |
24	| "12,000 of 200,000 tokens · 6%" | Once the model's window is known. The percentage shows at most one decimal. It can read "0 of …" for a moment after your first message, before the first response. |
25	| "12,000 tokens (window size unknown)" | Anthropic didn't report the window size. |
26	
27	When the inspector is narrow the figure shortens to "12,000 / 200,000 · 6%" or "6%", or to "12,000 tokens" with no known window. The tooltip always has the full figure.
28	
29	The bar under the figure fills in the accent colour and turns coral past 80%.
30	
31	**Clear** (↺), at the end of the row, puts the count back to zero, and so does a change of key or model, because each ends the conversation.
32	
33	## The settings
34	
35	Both settings are in **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**. A change applies without **Save** and keeps the conversation going. A new threshold counts from the end of the current turn, and a change to clearing applies from your next message.
36	
37	| Setting | What it does | Default | Range |
38	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
39	| **Compact when context reaches** … **tokens** | Replaces the conversation with a summary at the end of a turn. | On, 300,000 tokens | 20,000 to 900,000 tokens |
40	| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop older tool results from what the model sees. | Off | |
41	
42	The token field is dimmed while **Compact when context reaches** is off. A number outside the range beeps, and the field goes back to the stored value.
43	
44	## Compaction
45	
46	With **Compact when context reaches** on, the conversation is replaced by a summary at the end of the first turn that reaches the threshold. It never happens in the middle of a turn, and a [stopped](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) turn doesn't compact.
47	
48	The summary is asked to keep:
49	
50	- what you asked for and every preference you stated
51	- the project and any nest open
52	- the clips, tracks, markers and media involved
53	- the edits made, in order, and which were undone
54	- what's still open or was promised
55	
56	Rendered frames don't survive, so the summary describes in words what each one showed. The Assistant renders again when it needs to look.
57	
58	The transcript notes each step:
59	
60	| The transcript says | What it means |
61	| --- | --- |
62	| "Compacting the conversation (*N* tokens)…" | The summary has been asked for. |
63	| "Compacted: *N* → about *M* tokens. Earlier renders are gone; the assistant re-renders when it needs to look." | It worked. The Context meter drops to about *M*. |
64	| "Compaction didn't finish (*reason*); it will try again after the next turn." | No summary came back. The conversation is unchanged. |
65	
66	The summary request is priced like any other response, and it's part of that turn's [`Cost:` line](/assistant/cost/#per-turn).
67	
68	:::tip
69	Compaction only starts once the conversation reaches the threshold, so the threshold has to be lower than the model's window. If the Context meter shows a window smaller than your threshold, lower it.
70	:::
71	
72	## With compaction off
73	
74	Nothing replaces the conversation, so it keeps growing until it fills the model's window. From then on each message fails, with an [error in the transcript](/assistant/conversation/#errors), until you click **Clear**. **Clear** ends the conversation, and nothing of it carries into the next message.
75	
76	## Clearing old tool results
77	
78	A tool result is what comes back from one of the Assistant's tool calls, and a project's details can run long. With **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** on, Anthropic may drop older ones from what the model sees once the conversation passes 150,000 tokens. It's a lighter step than compaction: the conversation stays, and only old tool results go.
79	
80	- It keeps the five most recent tool uses.
81	- It clears at least 50,000 tokens at a time.
82	- It can happen in the middle of a turn.
83	- It never clears tool search results, which are how the Assistant finds its tools.
84	
85	Each clearing adds a note to the transcript, "Cleared *N* old tool results (*M* tokens) from the model's view." The model may have to fetch something again afterwards.
86	
87	Each clearing costs a fresh prompt-cache write: Anthropic can't reuse its stored copy of the conversation, so it stores a new one, and that goes on your bill. That's why it clears in large pieces.

2	title: "What it costs"
3	description: See what the Assistant costs per turn, per conversation and per month, and how far to trust the figures.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	The Assistant runs on your own Anthropic API key, so Anthropic bills you directly for what it uses. Frame Job shows you an estimate of that cost for each turn, each conversation and each month.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant"
12	  keys="⌘,"
13	  where={['Inspector ▸ Assistant tab ▸ Spend', 'The Cost line at the end of each turn']}
14	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."
15	/>
16	
17	## Your own billing
18	
19	Every response is priced by Frame Job from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices, a public price table on GitHub. Every figure on this page is **Frame Job's own estimate**. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was actually billed.
20	
21	| Where | What it covers |
22	| --- | --- |
23	| The [`Cost:` line](#per-turn) in the transcript | One turn |
24	| The [**Spend** row](#per-conversation) in the tab | The conversation so far |
25	| The [month's line](#per-month) in Settings | The current calendar month, across every window |
26	
27	## Per turn
28	
29	Each turn ends with a line in the transcript. For example:
30	
31	`Cost: $0.0182 · Frame Job's estimate at LiteLLM prices (cached 2026-10-25)`
32	
33	The amount sums every response in the turn, the [compaction](/assistant/context-and-compaction/#compaction) summary included. It shows to four decimal places, and a tiny positive amount reads "under $0.0001". A turn with no response has no `Cost:` line.
34	
35	The brackets name the price table and its date:
36	
37	| The brackets say | The prices came from |
38	| --- | --- |
39	| "bundled table of …" | The copy built into the app |
40	| "cached …" | The copy Frame Job keeps, from an earlier refresh |
41	| "fetched …" | A copy downloaded for this conversation |
42	
43	If a refresh failed, the brackets add "; not refreshed:" and the reason. A table that downloaded but couldn't be saved adds "; the price cache could not be written:" and the reason.
44	
45	## Unpriced responses
46	
47	A response that couldn't be priced shows as unknown with its reason, never as $0. In the `Cost:` line it reads "unknown (*reason*)", followed by "· at least $…" for the part that could be priced.
48	
49	A response goes unpriced when:
50	
51	- its model isn't in the price table, for example "*model* is not in the price table"
52	- the table lists the model but has no rate for what was used
53	- it used fast mode, for example `speed "fast" is not priced`
54	- it used a batch or priority tier
55	- it was a US-only request
56	
57	When a request sends more than 200,000 tokens, the model's higher rates apply if the table lists them.
58	
59	## Responses cut short
60	
61	A response cut short by [Stop](/assistant/stop-a-turn/) or an error is priced from what had arrived. It shows as "at least $… (a response was cut short)".
62	
63	## Per conversation
64	
65	The **Spend** row, under **Context** in the Assistant tab, adds up the conversation's turns since the last **Clear**, or since a key or model change ended the conversation.
66	
67	| The row reads | When |
68	| --- | --- |
69	| "Nothing yet" | Before the first response. |
70	| "$0.0532 · Frame Job's estimate" | Every response was priced. |
71	| "at least $… · Frame Job's estimate" | A response was cut short or couldn't be priced. Shortened to "≥$… · Frame Job's estimate" when the inspector is narrow. |
72	| "under $0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate" | A tiny positive amount. Shortened to `<$0.0001 · Frame Job's estimate` when narrow. |
73	| "unknown · Frame Job's estimate" | Nothing could be priced, or a response has no price and the priced part is under $0.00005. |
74	
75	Hovering the figure shows "What this conversation's responses cost at LiteLLM prices, as Frame Job estimates it. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."
76	
77	The figure is held in memory. If the helper, the small program that talks to Anthropic, stops, the row carries on from where it was.
78	
79	## Per month
80	
81	In **Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant**, a line under **Save** and **Remove** totals what the Assistant has cost in the current calendar month. The month runs in UTC, so it can turn over before or after midnight where you are.
82	
83	A response here is one reply from Anthropic, so one turn can count as several, and a compaction summary counts as one.
84	
85	| The line reads | When |
86	| --- | --- |
87	| "October 2026 (UTC): $1.24 over 87 responses." | Every response was priced. |
88	| "Nothing recorded in October 2026 (UTC)." | No responses this month. |
89	| "October 2026 (UTC): 5 responses; none could be priced." | No response had a price. |
90	| "October 2026 (UTC): 87 responses; 3 could not be priced, the rest came to $0.80." | Some had no price. They're counted, never added as $0. |
91	| "Reading the spend ledger…" | The [ledger](#the-spend-ledger) is being read. |
92	| "The spend ledger could not be read: *reason*." | It couldn't be read. |
93	| "This launch keeps no spend ledger." | Frame Job has no folder to keep one in. |
94	
95	Totals are rounded to the cent, and a positive amount that would round to $0.00 reads "under $0.01". When some lines of the ledger are damaged, the line adds a sentence such as "2 ledger lines could not be read." That count covers the whole ledger, because a line with no readable time can't be placed in a month.
96	
97	The line refreshes when Settings opens, and after each response while Settings is visible. During a refresh after a response, the last sentence stays until the new one is ready.
98	
99	Under it, a faint note says: "Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."
100	
101	## Prices refreshed daily
102	
103	Frame Job prices from LiteLLM's published Anthropic prices. It has a table built into the app, and keeps a copy refreshed at most once a day at `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/anthropic-prices.json`.
104	
105	A refresh is checked when a conversation starts, with a 30-second limit, and a turn keeps the prices it started with. The download is a plain request to `raw.githubusercontent.com`, made by the helper. It carries no key and no project data.
106	
107	If it fails, Frame Job prices from the cached copy or the built-in table, and the `Cost:` line says which it used.
108	
109	## The spend ledger
110	
111	The figures in Settings come from a ledger, `spend.jsonl` in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`. It's on your Mac, and only your account can read it.
112	
113	Each response is one line, with its time, the service, the model, the token counts, its speed and service tier, the prices used, and the dollars or why they're unknown. It never records your key or the conversation's content.
114	
115	If a response's cost can't be written, the transcript notes it once per conversation: "The spend ledger *path* could not be written: *reason*." That response is then missing from the month's total in Settings.
116

4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	The Assistant works by sending your conversation to Anthropic, so it's worth knowing what that includes. Frame Job has no account or relay of its own: what you send goes to Anthropic under your own key, and nowhere else.
9

12	  needs="An Anthropic API key. See Set up the Assistant."

14	
15	## What goes to Anthropic
16	
17	When you use the Assistant, these go to Anthropic under your key:
18	
19	- **Your messages**, and a short block in front of each one: the project's name and path, the open nest, the playhead and the selection.
20	- **What the tools send back**: the project's details as JSON, including media file paths, any clip transcripts it reads, the reason when something couldn't be done, and other results.
21	- **The frames it renders** to look at the picture.
22	
23	What it costs is billed to your key. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).
24	
25	Your key is handed straight to the helper, the small program Frame Job runs to talk to Anthropic. It isn't placed on a command line or in the helper's environment.
26	
27	When a conversation starts, the helper also asks Anthropic for the model's context window, under your key. That request names only the model.
28	
29	The Assistant [asks before](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-asks-about-first) it exports a movie or captions, saves the project or consolidates media. Other tools can still [write files without asking](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#file-writes-that-do-not-ask).
30	
31	## No audio to the cloud transcriber
32	
33	Audio never goes to the cloud transcriber from the Assistant. [Cloud transcription is withheld](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#tools-it-will-not-call), so uploading audio stays your choice, in **File ▸ Generate Captions…** or **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**.
34	
35	## The price table download
36	
37	Once a day at most, the helper downloads LiteLLM's public price table from GitHub. That request carries no key and no project data. See [Prices refreshed daily](/assistant/cost/#prices-refreshed-daily).
38	
39	## What stays on your Mac
40	
41	Everything else stays on your Mac. The Assistant keeps these files in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/`:
42	
43	| File | What it is |
44	| --- | --- |
45	| `anthropic-key` | Your key, in a file only you can read. |
46	| `spend.jsonl` | The [spend ledger](/assistant/cost/#the-spend-ledger). It holds token counts and dollars, never your key or the conversation's content. |
47	| `anthropic-prices.json` | The cached price table. |
48	
49	## The conversation lives in memory
50	
51	The conversation is kept in memory only, and goes when you clear it or close the window. Nothing of it is saved in the project or in the spend ledger.
